Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Renewables's results for the Q3. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Liam Greer, Chief Sustainability Officer; Tara Novak, Chief Operating Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Nina Kowalski, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the Q3. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance: our standout storage deployments and hybrid project updates, explosive revenue and earnings growth, impressive construction progress and commercial operation dates, exciting new PPAs secured along with favorable average PPA pricing, the meaningful impact of government incentives and subsidies, robust development pipeline additions and project milestones, strengthening gross margin and operating margin trends, and disciplined capital expenditure and operating expense management. These elements collectively underscore our momentum in scaling clean energy solutions amid surging demand from electrification, data centers, and decarbonization.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Our financial performance in the Q3 was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.25 billion, representing a 48% increase compared to the same period last year and 22% sequential growth from Q2. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning, increased energy production, and surging demand across our high-efficiency solar PV modules, next-gen BESS, and green hydrogen electrolyzers. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency, cost management, and scale benefits. Operating expenses totaled $312 million, primarily due to targeted investments in R&D, sales and marketing, and O&M optimization. Net income was $180 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $5.6-5.8 billion and earnings accordingly.

Let me break down the revenue and earnings growth in more detail. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $285 million, up 62% year-over-year, with margins expanding 320 basis points to 22.8%—our highest in three years. These results mark our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue expansion, fueled by volume growth, pricing discipline, and operational leverage from our scaled manufacturing. Solar PV contributed $775 million or 62% of revenue, up 55% YoY with 4.2 GWdc shipments, led by Gen-4 TOPCon modules at 24.5% efficiency winning utility-scale bids. Energy storage added $300 million, up 42%, with 2.8 GWh deployments and AI-optimized EMS boosting efficiency to 96.5%. Green hydrogen and emerging tech brought $175 million, up 28%, with 150 MW electrolyzer deployments.

Gross margins hit 29.8% consolidated, up 450 basis points sequentially and 620 basis points YoY, trending toward our 32-35% target. Solar PV manufacturing at 31.2% benefited from vertical integration, U.S. gigafactories qualifying for 45X credits worth $0.12/W, and polysilicon costs at $8.5/kg. Storage margins rose to 27.5% with LFP cell costs down 22% to $0.052/Wh. Offshore wind held at 22.4% despite steel inflation. Operating margins reached 14.2%, with OpEx at 15.6% of revenue, driven by R&D at 4.2% yielding perovskite tandems at 32.5% efficiency and SG&A efficiencies post-acquisitions.

Our CAPEX and OPEX details further highlight discipline. We deployed $685 million in Q2 CAPEX toward our $2.5 billion FY24 guidance, up 25% YoY for pipeline buildout. Solar took 45% for Desert Bloom completion, offshore wind 30% for Moray Firth, storage 20% for 1.2 GWh BESS, and manufacturing/R&D 5% for perovskite fabs. OPEX was $312 million, up 4% YoY on 22% revenue growth, with O&M at 42% reduced by drone analytics, SG&A at 28%, R&D 22% on hybrids and H2, yielding EBITDA margins of 42%. OPEX per MWh fell 11% to $12.50, with fleet availability at 98.2%.

A cornerstone is our storage deployment and hybrid updates. In Q3, we achieved commercial operation on 650 MW / 2,600 MWh standalone BESS across three projects, totaling 2.8 GW / 11.2 GWh YTD, up 180% from Q3 2023. These long-duration 4-hour assets use LFP cathodes from CATL and EVE, with 92.5% round-trip efficiency via our ApexFlow BMS featuring AI thermal management for over 7,000 cycles. Viper Storage (300 MW / 1,200 MWh) in ERCOT generates 45% from arbitrage ($200/MWh spreads), 35% ancillaries, 20% capacity. Pipeline at 8.2 GW / 33 GWh, 4.1 GW NTP soon, 55% U.S., 25% Australia, 20% Europe. Hybrids at 65% of 15 GW pipeline; energized 1.2 GW including 500 MWdc solar + 200 MW/800 MWh in California (38% capacity factor) and 400 MW wind + 150 MW/600 MWh in SPP ($55/MWh PPA). FY24 guidance: 3.5-4.0 GW storage, $450-500M hybrid backlog.

New PPAs secured totaled 1.4 GW across six projects, lifting contracted backlog to 8.2 GW, up 25% YoY. Highlights: 500 MW solar+storage with Microsoft in ERCOT, 300 MW with AWS in CAISO, 400 MW with SCE, 200 MW Duke, 100 MW Orsted VPPA. Blended average PPA price $26/MWh LCOE-adjusted, flat sequentially; U.S. Southwest $24/MWh, CAISO $29/MWh, Europe $32/MWh. Resilience from AI design, agrivoltaics, 80% BESS inclusion for 15-20% uplift, LCOE $18/MWh.

Government incentives contributed $187 million or 22% of revenue, boosting EBITDA by $142 million. IRA ITC/PTC at 65%, with 10% domestic/energy community adders; $320M monetized via transferability. Europe REPowerEU up to 35% capex via Innovation Fund. APAC PLI $5.4M/GW. Only 35% pipeline subsidy-reliant; guiding $750-850M in FY25.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Thornton to discuss our project development activities.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We added a record 4.2 GW in Q3, bringing early/mid-stage to 12.8 GW, up 32% QoQ. Solar 2.8 GW, wind 800 MW, BESS/hybrids 600 MW/2.4 GWh. U.S. 2.9 GW (ERCOT/CAISO), Europe 900 MW (UK/Germany), international 400 MW (Australia/India). Hit 15 milestones advancing 3.1 GW to shovel-ready: entitlements for 450 MW Rio Sol hybrid (Meta PPA $28/MWh), 1.8 GW PPAs (Microsoft Prairie Wind $32/MWh), FERC/SPP approvals, FID on 400 MW/1.6 GWh BESS, groundbreak on 350 MW Desert Bloom, energized 100 MW/400 MWh BESS.

On construction, over 4.2 GW under construction. U.S.: Desert Bloom Solar 82% complete (Q4 first energy, year-end COD, $45/MWh PPA), Brazos Wind 65% (Q2 2025 COD), Horizon Peak BESS 92% (Aug 2024 COD). Europe: North Sea Vanguard 45% (H2 2027 COD). APAC: Mekong floating solar 55% (Q3 2025 COD). Expect 2.5 GW CODs 2024-2025, $450M EBITDA. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect substantial new projects online soon, plus strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts focus on enhancing efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewables. Significant breakthroughs include advanced solar panels like perovskite-silicon tandems at 28-32.5% efficiency, LFP BESS with AI EMS at 96.5% RTE, ApexFlow BMS, ApexOptimize for multi-market stacking (18% revenue uplift), and H2-Optima electrolyzers at 70 kW/m². Our vertically integrated platform ensures IRA domestic content for full ITC, with sodium-ion pilots targeting 20% cost cuts by 2027. These will revolutionize the energy landscape.

Next, Liam Greer will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Liam Greer:
Thank you, Elena. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have ambitious goals for reducing carbon emissions—targeting net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2030—improving energy efficiency across assets, and responsible resource management, including water recycling in solar farms and biodiversity enhancements via agrivoltaics. Community engagement includes local hiring (30% workforce) and H2 hubs support. Our degradation rates at 1.2% annually and 99.5% availability reflect this.

Now, Tara Novak will provide operational highlights.

Tara Novak:
Thank you, Liam. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We optimize operations via best-in-class asset management, predictive maintenance with drones and NexOS platform (18% downtime cut), and supply chain resilience (95% localization). Heavy investment in employee training ensures excellence, with fleet CUF uplifts to 38-52% in hybrids and O&M costs down to $22/kW-year for wind.

Raj Patel, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Tara. We are executing our long-term plan: expanding in key markets like U.S. Southwest and Europe, diversifying into green hydrogen and carbon capture, strengthening partnerships (e.g., Transgrid, Orsted). Vertical integration at 40% self-supply, $500M FY24 capex for 10 GWh BESS and tandems, targeting LCOE <$20/MWh by 2025. Corporate PPAs now 45% backlog.

And finally, Nina Kowalski, can you address our risk management strategies?

Nina Kowalski:
Thank you, Raj. We have robust strategies mitigating market volatility (70% hedged PPAs), regulatory risks (FERC reforms, policy cliffs stress-tested at 8-10% EBITDA hit), environmental risks (flood/DOD modeling), and supply chain (2 GW module bank). Continuous monitoring, 3.2x net debt/EBITDA, $2.5B liquidity, DSCR 1.8x provide buffers. Interconnection exposure down to 15%, lobbying via SEIA/GWEC.

I'll turn it back to Jordan for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you all. In conclusion, Apex Renewables had a truly exceptional Q3. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, commitment to innovation, and focus on sustainability will drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, John. Green hydrogen is a priority in our emerging tech segment, contributing 14% of Q3 revenue with 150 MW PEM electrolyzer deployments, including a 50 MW off-take with partners for EU markets. We're scaling Fab-3 in Texas to 85% utilization with IRA credits, piloting 50 MW at Desert Bloom with ITM Power stacks for California's H2 hubs by 2026. FY24 capex includes $69M R&D for H2-Optima at 70 kW/m² density, co-located on 200 MW wind sites in Australia tapping the $100B global market. Partnerships with Plug Power and NREL de-risk scale-up, targeting LCOE below $2/kg by 2027 via tandem PV integration. This diversifies beyond solar/storage, with 28% YoY growth and pilots qualifying for DOE LSAM grants.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Jordan Hale:
Great question, Emily. Competition is intensifying with Chinese oversupply and peers like NextEra scaling, but our edge lies in U.S.-centric vertical integration (85% domestic content for full IRA ITC/45X), proprietary tech like ApexOptimize yielding 18% revenue uplift, and 12 GW backlog at $18B value providing 3x FY25 visibility. We've pruned queues, fast-tracked 1.5 GW PJM via FERC 2023, and shifted to hybrids (65% pipeline) for 12%+ IRRs. Corporate offtakers at 45% reduce utility risk, while perovskite tandems and sodium-ion keep LCOE 15% below peers. Q3 module ASPs held amid $0.18/W dumping via locked offtakes. Long-term, 20-25% EBITDA CAGR positions us strongly.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

Nina Kowalski:
Thanks, David. Climate change poses risks like extreme weather, but we've embedded resilience: elevated moorings for 1-in-50 floods in Mekong, LiDAR micro-siting for karst in Texas, black-start BESS for grid resilience. Degradation managed at 1.2% annual via predictive modeling. Opportunities outweigh: data center demand drives hybrids, IRA energy communities adder boosts IRRs. Stress tests show 5-7% EBITDA sensitivity to +2°C scenarios, mitigated by diversification (U.S. 52%, Europe 28%), insurance, and VPPs. We're piloting vanadium flow for duck curve and carbon capture tie-ins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Sarah Chen:
Excellent point, Lisa. Long-term profitability is robust, with portfolio IRR at 12.5% above 10% hurdle, ROIC 18.2%, EBITDA CAGR 20-25% through decade per BNEF $1T storage TAM. Backlog at 8.2 GW contracted yields $450M annual EBITDA at stabilization, LCOE $18-25/MWh unsubsidized beating coal. Hybrids deliver 38-52% capacity factors, stacking revenues (arbitrage 45%, ancillaries 35%). IRA extensions, 85% repeat O&M (20% recurring), 95% utilization drive 42% EBITDA margins by 2025. Risks like rates hedged 80% fixed, merchant upside in ERCOT/CAISO. FY25 guide: $750-850M incentives, Q3 revenue $1.4-1.5B, EPS $2.85-3.00.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Apex Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
